zh.title: 从四个点出发——K4 单元框架
zh.description: 一个仅有四个顶点的有限量子对象，不含任何连续拟合参数，涵盖十一项物理机制推导。它给出 μ 子—电子质量比的 15 位候选数值，现有实验分辨至前 8 位且 8 位全部吻合。此为回顾性对照，而非预注册预测。未经同行评议，公开审阅中。

hero.glyphA: 四个顶点、六条连线、三种颜色
hero.glyphB: 每条连线要求两端异色，必有一对顶点同色相撞
hero.glyphAlt: 动态示意：一个四面体，四个顶点各着一色，仅使用三种颜色与六条棱。每一帧都至少有一条棱两端同色，并以高亮闪烁标示。它并非三维空间中的几何体，仅用于表示点与点之间的相互作用规则。

why.h2: 物理学尚不知晓，宇宙为何偏偏取这些数值。
why.lede: 基础物理中约有二十余个基本常数。它们共同决定了原子的尺度与宇宙膨胀的速率。现行物理学通过实验逐一测定这些数值——电子质量、电磁相互作用强度、暗物质密度——再将其作为外部参数手动写入方程。
why.contrast: 标准模型包含二十余个由实验测定的自由参数；而本框架没有任何可连续调节的拟合旋钮。
why.contrastNote: 具体而言：最简标准模型含 19 个自由参数；计入中微子质量后增至 26 到 28 个，取决于中微子是狄拉克型还是马约拉纳型。宇宙学模型还需另行引入若干参数。
why.noKnob: 不含连续拟合参数的计算一旦与实验不符，便没有调参退路。模型中保留的仅是离散选择：采取哪条理论分支、将算出结果对应至哪一项物理观测量、按何种规则读数。每项离散选择均已在文档中明示，并标注为作者列出的开放接口。

object.h2: 四个顶点，六条连线，三种颜色，一条规则。
object.intro: 后文所呈现的所有物理数值，均由这同一数学对象导引而出——既考察单个孤立单元，也考察多个单元拼接而成的晶格网络。以下分三步简要说明。

beats.body: 四个顶点两两相连，共六条连线——图论中称为四顶点完全图 K₄。每个顶点设有一个仅含三种内部状态的三态量子开关（不妨喻为三种颜色）。每条连线仅施予一项反铁磁约束：两端状态尽量相异，若两端同色则记一次失配代价。关键随即出现：仅有三种颜色却要分配给四个顶点，无论如何排列，必定存在一对顶点同色。而完全图中任意两点间都有连线，因此同色失配必然存在。至于这一代价如何在量子力学中结算，详见第三步。请先留意两点：第一，这四个顶点并非现实空间中的位置坐标，三维空间在本框架中属于后续涌现结构；第二，物理世界对应于大量 K₄ 单元拼接而成的网络，具体拼接规则已被作者标注为条件性步骤。

beats.h3: 唯有关系具有物理意义
beats.body: 试想四位歌者合唱一个和弦：和弦之美不在某一个人的单音之中，而在于音与音之间的音程关系；四人同时移高音调，音程与和弦性质依然不变。此处亦然，且更为彻底：没有哪个顶点“绝对代表红色”。真正具有物理意义的仅是顶点之间的相对关系——是否同态，以及二者如何形成反对称或对称叠加。若同时置换所有顶点的三种颜色，系统哈密顿量、全部能级谱以及从中读出的一切比值都严格保持不变。不仅如此，即使将不同颜色状态在复线性空间中作连续幺正旋转，只要四个顶点同步变换，一切物理结构依旧不变。这种局部到整体的连续规范对称性，正是后续衍生出规范场的数学种子；而将这一内部对称性正式等同于强相互作用中的“色荷”，则是作者明确列为开放的一步。相互作用规则里没有任何一项指向单个顶点：六个相互作用项，各管一对顶点。

beats.h3: 基态必然处于量子阻挫叠加态
beats.body: 经典系统面对失配只能择一妥协：总得有一条连线发生同色碰撞，最优经典排布的能量记账仍为 +1。但量子系统可以构造经典世界无法实现的相干叠加——在振幅间引入正负号相位。相互作用规则评估每条连线时，本质上相当于考察对调两端状态后波函数的符号响应：经典构型中两端同色计 +1、异色计 0；而量子叠加态可将两端锁入交换反对称的单态关系，从而取得 −1 的负能量收益。系统的最低能量层（基态）正是由此类单态叠加构成：它仅利用那 36 种仅出现一次同色碰撞的构型，将基态总能量压低至 −2，比最优经典排布整整低出 3 个能量单位。这并非把失配平均摊薄（经典混合态的能量下限仍为 +1）。更关键的是，如此能量简并的基态并非唯一，而是九重简并（9 = 3 × 3）：前一个“3”来自三种颜色状态，后一个“3”来自四个顶点置换对称性下的三个独立表示方向。九重基态作为一个整体，对六条连线完全一视同仁（每条边平均分摊 −1/3），而单个基态自身在各边上又呈现差异化取向——阻挫始终存在，整个基态层却不偏袒任何一条边。其中的第二个“3”，即为本框架内物质“三代”结构的代数起源；将这一“3”真正落实为时空中的三代夸克与轻子，已被作者标注为开放步骤。由于真正基态是 81 种经典构型上的九维叠加子空间，系统永不会坍缩到 81 种经典状态中的某单一构型。

object.forced: 这一基本对象的全部结构特征并非随意拼凑。在作者所界定的对象范畴内——每点一个三态开关、仅限两两成对相互作用——四个顶点、三种颜色、完全图拓扑、交换型耦合以及偏向异色的反铁磁符号，皆由数学自洽性唯一逼定。整套理论唯一的物理前提是：存在此类 K₄ 单元并构成了晶格网络。之所以必定是四个顶点，是因为量子力学中的虚数单位 i 满足 i² = −1，几何上对应于四分之一圈（90°）旋转——连转两次恰好构成 180° 反向（乘以 −1）；三顶点或五顶点回路的单步旋转分别为 120° 与 72°，均无法两次旋转得到 −1。之所以必定是三种颜色，则是基于手征区分准则，颜色数需为奇数（偶数会混入无法区分手征的实要素）、至少为三且少于顶点数。该前提范畴究竟有多宽泛，作者已专列为审阅问题之一；在范畴内部，上述核心条款均已通过形式化定理证明器 Lean 核验，零未完成证明步骤（零 sorry）。
object.twoMinutes: 只要数清四个顶点、六条连线与三种颜色，您便已亲自验证了上述自举定理的图论部分。

object.gridIntro: 总计仅 81 种构型，足以全部展现。以下画出施加相互作用规则之前的每一种经典配色，以四面体示意，加粗连线表示两端同色。

object.gridSweepDone: 已遍历全部 81 种构型：无一不含同色连线，每一种都至少存在一条加粗边。
object.gridSweepResult: 81 种构型中命中数为 0。四个顶点仅配三种颜色时，必有一对顶点颜色相同；而完全图中任意两点均有连线相连，同色边必然出现。规则无法在所有边上同时满足，物理学称之为阻挫（frustration）。在这里，阻挫不是人为假设，而是组合算术。

object.gridCaveat: 此 81 幅图为未施规则前的经典基态构型。真实量子基态并非其中任何单一构型，而是带正负相位的九重简并叠加态（见第三步）。此处尚未涉及实验物理推导，仅用以明示状态总数及阻挫的结构必然性。
object.countsCaption: 四个顶点、六条连线、每顶点三种颜色：施加规则前共 3⁴ = 81 种经典构型。

checkIt.body: 跨代夸克混合幅度在物理学中称为卡比博参数（Cabibbo parameter）。在本框架内，该数值并非经验拟合小数，而是精确有理分数 9/40。直接验算可知：9 ÷ 40 = 0.225，三位即告除尽，后续诸位皆为零。实验测量值为 0.22501 ± 0.00068，两者在现有精度内完全一致。
checkIt.after: 9/40 是模型结构给出的精确有理数，而非连续调参的结果。但要断言这一分数就是实验测量的卡比博参数，中间仍须依赖物理嵌入假设——作者已将这一映射步骤列为开放接口。
checkIt.tierChip: 条件性 · 嵌入至实测物理量的步骤已列为开放接口
checkIt.containsLabel: 0.225 落于实验误差范围之内

second.body: 电磁作用与弱作用的混合比例称为弱混合角。其理论裸值同样是一个精确分数 3/13——指未计入能标跑动效应前的源头参数值。3/13 并不直接与实验值比对；实验室读出须由该裸值出发，依据固定的重整化换算规则跑动至 Z 玻色子质量能标，其中包含的两项小修正亦由理论完全定死。最终算得 0.231219995，实验测量为 0.23122 ± 0.00006：前四位完全吻合，后续五位有待未来更高精度电弱实验检验。而将比值中的两项结构正式认同为物理上的电磁力与弱力，仍依托于作者标注的两条开放接口。

en.title: An object with only four points — K4 Cell Framework
en.description: One four-point quantum object, zero continuous fitted parameters, eleven whys. It produces a 15-digit candidate value for m_μ/m_e; experiment resolves 8 digits and all 8 agree. A retrospective comparison, not a preregistered prediction. Not peer reviewed.

brand.name: K4 Cell
brand.tagline: From four points to nature’s constants

hero.h1a: A four-point object yields a 15-digit value for the muon-to-electron mass ratio.
hero.h1b: Experiment currently resolves 8 digits. All 8 agree.
hero.sub: The Standard Model takes these numbers as inputs. K4 aims to make them consequences of geometry.
hero.rulerLabel: m_μ/m_e · computed against measured, digit by digit
hero.rulerAlt: Digit-by-digit comparison. The computed m_μ/m_e is 206.768282688691, fifteen significant digits. The measured value, 206.7682827, resolves only the first 8. All 8 agree; seven more digits lie past the cut, waiting to be checked.
hero.bet: If inverted neutrino mass ordering is established, the normal-ordering claim used here and the conclusions that depend on it must be revised.
hero.betNote: JUNO is running; Hyper-K targets 2028; DUNE targets 2029 for its first far detector and 2031 for beam.
byline: Zhihua Liang · PhD in Physics (Southern Methodist University, 2012) · BSc in Physics (Tsinghua University, 2003)
ATLAS collaboration 2006–2012 (H→WW analysis) · INFN Cagliari / CERN LHCb 2024–2026
1003-page monograph, frozen 2026-07-08 · not peer reviewed · as of 2026-11-19: 1 standalone paper in review, 1 revised for transfer
hero.glyphA: Four points, six links, three colours
hero.glyphB: Every link wants its two ends to differ, and one pair always clashes
hero.glyphAlt: Animation: a tetrahedron, each of its four vertices in one of only three colours, six edges. In every frame at least one edge joins two vertices of the same colour, and that edge flickers. Not a shape in space; only a drawing of which points have a rule between them.

why.h2: Nobody knows why the universe runs on the numbers it runs on.
why.lede: There are about twenty of these numbers. They set the size of an atom and the rate the universe is flying apart. Physics measures each one — the electron’s mass, how strongly light grips charge, how much of the universe is dark matter — writes it into the equations by hand, and moves on.
why.contrast: The Standard Model has about twenty dials, each turned into place by experiment. Here there are none.
why.contrastNote: About twenty: 19 in the minimal Standard Model; 26 to 28 once neutrino masses are included, depending on whether neutrinos are Dirac or Majorana. Cosmology adds a batch of its own.
why.noKnob: A calculation with no dial to turn is wrong when it is wrong; there is no way back. “Dial” here means a continuous one. The freedom that remains is discrete — which branch, which way a computed number is fastened onto a measured quantity, which channel to read on. Each of them is stated in the open, and each carries an interface the author lists as open.
dials: how far quarks stray between generations
the recipe mixing electromagnetism and the weak force
how strong the strong force is
whether the strong force breaks CP
how fast the universe flies apart

object.h2: Four points, six links, three colours, one rule.
object.intro: Every number below is read off this one object — alone, and glued to many copies of itself. Here it is, in three steps, ninety seconds.

beats.body: Four points, every pair joined: six links. Graph theory calls that the complete graph on four points, K₄. On each point sits a tiny quantum switch with three settings; call them three colours. Each link asks one thing: that its two ends differ. A link whose ends match is charged once. Now the key step: with only three colours, four points cannot all differ. Some pair always matches. And because every pair is joined, that matching pair has a link between them. So the rule can never be kept everywhere at once: however the four points are coloured, some link is charged. How that bill is finally settled comes in the third step. Two things to hold on to. First, the four points are not four places in space; space, in this theory, grows later. Second, the universe is not one tetrahedron but many of them glued together; how they glue is a step the author marks conditional.

Think of four singers holding a chord. What you hear is in no single voice; a held note alone is not a chord. Transpose all four together and the chord does not change, because only the intervals are audible. Here it is the same, and it goes further: no point is really red. What carries meaning is the relation between two points — whether they match, and how the pair is combined. Swap every colour at once and the energy, the whole ladder of energy levels, and every number the theory reads from the object stay exactly as they were. And it is more than renaming: blend red and green in any proportion into two new colours, do it at all four points together, and still nothing changes. That continuous turning-together is the seed from which a gauge field grows further downstream, a gauge field being the kind of field that carries a force. That part comes later. Matching that field to the colour of the strong force is a step the author lists as open. Not one term of the rule names a single point: six terms, one per pair.

The classical world must choose: this link clashes, or that one. Some link has to lose, and even the best arrangement is charged +1. The quantum world can do one thing the classical world cannot: hold different pictures together with plus and minus signs. The rule scores a link by asking, in effect, “what happens if I swap your two ends?” In a classical picture a match scores +1 and a difference 0. A quantum state can hold the two ends in a combination that changes sign under the swap, and that relation scores below zero, one step beyond merely different. The lowest-energy state, the ground state, is built exactly so. It uses only the 36 pictures with a single clash, and the total is −2, three whole units below the best honest classical arrangement. This is not the loss spread thin; a spread-out mixture would still score +1. And there is not one such ground state but nine: 9 = 3 × 3, three colours times three independent ways of labelling the four points. Taken together, the nine treat the six links alike — each link carries −1/3; taken one at a time, no two links are alike. The clash is always there, and the ground level as a whole favours no link over another. That second three is where this framework’s three generations come from — the fact that the electron has two heavier copies, and each quark two more. Carrying that three onto spacetime is a step the author marks open. The object is then in none of the 81 pictures, and it never will pick one. It never settles, not because it is moving, but because it refuses to choose.

object.forced: The shape of this object was not chosen. Four points, three colours, the complete graph, one coupling (one and the same strength on all six links), the antiferromagnetic sign (matching costs, differing is free) — within the class the framework states, each is a theorem forced by self-consistency. The one thing assumed is that a lattice of such cells exists: many of these four-point units glued together. Four points, because i — the number school defines by i² = −1 — is a quarter turn: turn twice and you are facing backwards, which is what multiplying by −1 does. With three points a step is a third of a turn, with five a fifth, and two steps of either never turn you around. Three colours, because on the author’s own criterion the number must be odd, at least three, and fewer than the points. How wide that stated class is, the author has put up for review himself. Closed; the core clauses are checked in Lean, a program that verifies a proof step by step. A step a proof leaves unproved has to be marked sorry; here there are none.
object.twoMinutes: Count: four points, six links, three colours — you have just reproduced the graph-theory half of the theorem above.
object.gridIntro: There are only 81 — few enough to print every one. Below is every picture before the rule is applied, drawn as a tetrahedron with one colour per point. Thick lines join two points that share a colour.
object.gridSweep: Find a picture with no repeated colour
object.gridSweepDone: Swept all 81 pictures. None is free of a same-colour link; every one shows at least one thick line.
object.gridSweepResult: Zero out of 81. With four points and only three colours, two points must share a colour, and every pair is linked, so that link is there. Physicists have a name for a rule that cannot be kept everywhere at once: frustration. Here it is not an assumption. It is arithmetic.
object.gridMeanLabel: Same-colour links per picture, averaged over all 81
object.gridCaveat: These 81 are the pictures before the rule is applied. The ground state is none of them: it is a superposition carrying plus and minus signs, and there are nine of those, as in the third step. No physics is derived here; these pictures only fix how many basic pictures the object has, and show that the frustration is structural.
object.countsCaption: Four points, six links, three colours per point: 3⁴ = 81 basic pictures before the rule is applied.

checkIt.body: How far quarks stray between generations is what physics calls the Cabibbo parameter. In this framework it comes out not as a decimal but as an exact fraction: 9/40. Do the division. 9 ÷ 40 = 0.225, exactly; the division terminates, and past that point there are only zeros. The measured value is 0.22501 ± 0.00068. You have just checked one line of the table further down, by hand.
checkIt.after: 9/40 is an exact rational, not a decimal that was tuned. Fastening it to a measured quantity — saying “this is the Cabibbo parameter” — is the step the author lists as open.
checkIt.tierChip: Conditional · the step onto a measured quantity, which the author lists as open
checkIt.stepButton: Carry the division one digit further

second.body: The recipe mixing electromagnetism and the weak force is what physics calls the weak mixing angle. Its value at the source — before any translation to laboratory conditions — is another fraction: 3/13. That 3/13 is not the number compared with experiment. What the lab reads is worked out from it by a fixed conversion rule, carried to the mass of the Z boson, and the two small terms in that rule are fixed by the theory as well. The result is 0.231219995; measured, 0.23122 ± 0.00006. Four digits match; the next five are written for the future. That the two ingredients in that recipe really are electromagnetism and the weak force rests on two interfaces the author lists as open.

tiers.title: Every claim carries one small tag, in three tiers
key: Proved as mathematics, but only inside the scope it draws for itself; whether experiment has confirmed it is a separate question.
Derived, provided one named open interface — one unfinished step in the derivation — holds; it depends on no fitted parameter.
A one-sided limit, or a test the future will settle; sitting below every existing limit means untested, not confirmed.
